correctness.rationale: The exact binary deletion-shadow incidence program is equivalent to the list-decoding definition. All seven lower witnesses are independently checked against distinct output-parent incidence. All upper bounds follow from rational nonnegative dual weights at every leaf of a complete binary branching tree: one node each at n=1,...,6; 101 nodes/51 leaves at n=7. An independent 25-node/13-leaf tree proves unique-decoding capacity 16 at n=7. A standard-library verifier checks every fraction, residual capacity, branch and witness from certificate.json; no floating-point solver is trusted for the proof. No assertion is made for other n.

value.rationale: This is the first exact nondecomposable-optimum boundary in the natural two-list one-deletion packing problem: at lengths one through six two disjoint uniquely decodable VT classes attain capacity, while at length seven a 33-word code outperforms every union of two uniquely decodable codes (at most 32). The result is structural, motivated by the VT-union construction in current list-deletion literature, and includes an exact reproducible capacity benchmark rather than an arbitrary weak numerical improvement.
